summary: Since round 4, ExtensionHost now numbers its link lookups, so a slower, older lookup cannot overwrite links from a newer one. It also logs an unexpected rejection of the background refresh; I accept the coverage exemption for that line. The source logic is sound, but a workspace-server temp test now fails. It assumes the background link refresh has finished before the first `extensions.list()` call returns, which is a race. Because that run fails, the coverage gate also counts the appsRouter lines and ExtensionHost lines 118-122 and 126 as uncovered.

findings.body: The test assumes a background lookup has already finished. Since the F4 fix, `list()` starts `refreshRemoteLinks()` without waiting for it and answers from the links it already has. So the first `extensions.list()` after `addRemote` can still return the stored `https://stale.gethalo.dev/notes/view/`, and that happened in this run. This test failed, the workspace-server temp run exited 1, and the coverage gate counted appsRouter.ts lines 40, 44, 46, 50, 52 and 54-55 and ExtensionHost.ts lines 118-122 and 126 as uncovered. Make the test wait for the refresh. Either use `await expect.poll(async () => (await server.rpc.extensions.list())[0]?.url).toBe("https://old.gethalo.dev/notes/view/")`, or open the watch first and wait for the snapshot that carries the refreshed link. The fixed `setTimeout(50)` in the third test (line ~148) has the same timing problem and should poll too.

testRequests.target: packages/workspace-server/test/.tmp-tests/Publisher.test.ts:49 and the setTimeout wait near the end of the third test
testRequests.rationale: Replace the race with expect.poll or a watch snapshot. Then the workspace-server temp run passes reliably and covers appsRouter.ts:40-55 and ExtensionHost.ts:118-126.
